metadata.phase: Phase 1: Nutrition Dataset Research & Feasibility Audit
metadata.auditor_role: Senior Data Engineer & Full-Stack Software Architect

candidate_datasets.name: Indian Food Composition Tables (IFCT 2017)
candidate_datasets.publisher: National Institute of Nutrition (NIN), Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), Department of Health Research, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Govt. of India
candidate_datasets.api_documentation: No official REST API provided by ICMR-NIN. Community npm/deno package '@ifct2017/compositions' and GitHub 'nodef/ifct2017' provide parsed CSV/JSON tables.
candidate_datasets.energy_unit: Kilojoules (kJ) primary; kcal derived via Atwater factors (17 kJ/g protein, 17 kJ/g carb, 37 kJ/g fat, 8 kJ/g fibre)

nutrient_coverage.macronutrients: Moisture, Protein, Total Fat, Available Carbohydrates, Total Dietary Fibre (Insoluble & Soluble), Ash
nutrient_coverage.micronutrients: 151+ parameters including individual amino acids, fatty acid profiles, fat-soluble vitamins (A, D2, D3, E, K1, K2), water-soluble vitamins (B1, B2, B3, B5, B6, B7, B9, C), carotenoids, polyphenols, macrominerals, trace elements, heavy metals.

candidate_datasets.processing_state: Predominantly RAW agricultural commodities (534 raw ingredients, 8 cooked/processed entries limited to boiled eggs and roasted vermicelli).
candidate_datasets.recipe_and_portion_support: No prepared recipes (no idli, dosa, chapati, sambar, dal tadka, biryani). No household measures (cups/bowls/pieces). Provides edible portion cleaning yield factors and nutrient retention factors by cooking method.

license_and_legal.official_license: Copyright © National Institute of Nutrition (ICMR). Personal, academic, and non-commercial educational use permitted with attribution. Storing, reproducing, or redistributing electronically for commercial products requires explicit prior written permission from Director, NIN.
license_and_legal.community_parser_license: AGPL-3.0-or-later (current) / MIT (older releases) for parser code in 'nodef/ifct2017'. Note: Parser license does not override underlying ICMR-NIN data copyright.

candidate_datasets.api_limits_and_keys: N/A for flat files. Free offline SQLite/JSON access.
data_quality_issues: Edible Oils and Fats (T001-T014, including Ghee, Mustard oil, Coconut oil) report enerc = 0 kJ despite 100g total fat due to parser null-coercion/uncalculated source cells.
Energy is in kJ, not kcal. Failure to convert results in a ~4.184x calorie calculation error.
Zero cooked dishes and zero household portion sizes; unsuitable as a standalone consumer logging database without recipe engine and portion tables.
candidate_datasets.recommended_role: PRIMARY REFERENCE BENCHMARK for raw Indian ingredients, indigenous cultivars, and pulse/grain macronutrient baselines.

candidate_datasets.name: USDA FoodData Central (FDC)
candidate_datasets.publisher: Agricultural Research Service (ARS), United States Department of Agriculture (USDA)
candidate_datasets.record_count: >365,000 across all sub-databases (Foundation: ~2,000; SR Legacy: 8,789; FNDDS: ~7,000; Branded: >350,000)
candidate_datasets.food_categories: Comprehensive global agriculture, US survey foods, processed commodities, commercial foods
candidate_datasets.nutrient_basis: Per 100 grams, plus explicit gram weights for household portions (e.g. 1 cup, 1 piece, 1 slice, 1 tbsp)
candidate_datasets.energy_unit: Both kcal and kJ reported (Nutrient ID 1008: kcal, Nutrient ID 1062: kJ)

nutrient_coverage.macronutrients: Full proximate breakdown (Water, Protein, Total Lipid, Carbohydrate by difference, Total Dietary Fiber)
nutrient_coverage.micronutrients: Full mineral and vitamin spectrum, lipid classes, amino acids across Foundation and SR Legacy.

candidate_datasets.processing_state: Distinguishes RAW, BOILED, ROASTED, MICROWAVED, STEAMED, CANNED, and DEHYDRATED states with distinct FDC IDs.
candidate_datasets.recipe_and_portion_support: Excellent portion mapping via FoodPortions table in FNDDS and SR Legacy (gram weights for household measures). Survey (FNDDS) includes multi-ingredient cooked preparations.
candidate_datasets.publication_date: Updated semi-annually (April and October; current version October 2024)

license_and_legal.official_license: U.S. Public Domain / Creative Commons Zero (CC0 1.0 Universal Dedication).
license_and_legal.attribution_requirement: Requested but not legally binding: 'U.S. Department of Agriculture, Agricultural Research Service. FoodData Central. fdc.nal.usda.gov.'

candidate_datasets.api_limits_and_keys: Requires free Data.gov API key (1,000 requests/hour/IP). 'DEMO_KEY' allows 30-50 requests/hour but triggers HTTP 429 upon bursts. Bulk CSV/JSON downloads have no rate limits.
data_quality_issues: Inconsistent energy unit reporting across sub-databases: SR Legacy often returns energy in kJ under nutrient name 'Energy', while FNDDS and Branded report kcal.
Limited coverage of regional Indian culinary preparations (e.g. no Idli, Dosa, Sambar, Rasam, Pav Bhaji, Khichdi, Poha); western bias.
Branded sub-database contains crowdsourced/vendor label submissions with missing micronutrients and unvalidated serving sizes.
candidate_datasets.recommended_role: PRIMARY SYSTEM CORE for raw-vs-cooked conversion factors, standard portion gram weights, Western staples, global meats/poultry, and fallback nutritional values.

candidate_datasets.name: Open Food Facts (OFF) - India & Global
candidate_datasets.publisher: Open Food Facts Association (Non-profit community initiative)
formats: Daily/Monthly GZipped JSONL / CSV bulk dumps
candidate_datasets.record_count: >3.1 million global products; >24,800 products tagged for India (e.g. Amul, Britannia, Haldiram's, Nestle India, Parle, ITC, Mother Dairy)
candidate_datasets.food_categories: Packaged and commercial foods, beverages, dairy, snacks, ready-to-eat meals, packaged condiments
candidate_datasets.nutrient_basis: Per 100g / 100ml and per packaged serving (where specified on product label)
candidate_datasets.energy_unit: Reported in both kJ and kcal ('energy-kcal_100g', 'energy-kj_100g')

nutrient_coverage.macronutrients: Energy, Total Fat, Saturated Fat, Carbohydrates, Sugars, Dietary Fiber, Proteins, Salt / Sodium
nutrient_coverage.micronutrients: Sporadic; limited to mandatory front-of-package / nutrition panel declarations (e.g. Calcium, Vitamin D/A in fortified foods).

candidate_datasets.processing_state: Commercial ultra-processed, processed, and packaged foods (NOVA Class 3 and 4 predominantly).
candidate_datasets.recipe_and_portion_support: Serving size strings provided as printed on packaging (e.g. '30g', '1 biscuit (12.5g)', '1 pack (70g)'). No recipe-level ingredient breakdown.

license_and_legal.official_license: Open Database License (ODbL 1.0) for the database; Database Contents License (DbCL 1.0) for individual contents; Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike (CC-BY-SA 2.0) for product images.
license_and_legal.attribution_requirement: Mandatory: Must attribute Open Food Facts, provide a link to the database, and share back derivative database enhancements under ODbL.

candidate_datasets.api_limits_and_keys: Free public access without mandatory API key. Strict rate-limiting on complex search API queries (frequent HTTP 503 errors under load). Direct barcode lookup API (/api/v2/product/{barcode}.json) is high-performance.
data_quality_issues: Crowdsourced OCR data leads to data entry errors (e.g. 100g fat entering as 1000g, swapped carbohydrate and sugar fields).
Many entries have missing fiber, sodium, or micronutrient values.
Runtime full-text search API is throttled; production apps must ingest bulk dumps into a local PostgreSQL database rather than querying the live search endpoint.
candidate_datasets.recommended_role: SUPPLEMENTARY DATABASE for Indian packaged foods, barcode scanning (EAN-13/UPC), and branded packaged snacks/dairy.

candidate_datasets.name: RecipeDB / DietRx
candidate_datasets.publisher: Computational Gastronomy Lab, Indraprastha Institute of Information Technology Delhi (IIIT-Delhi) - Prof. Ganesh Bagler et al.
candidate_datasets.api_documentation: Academic research portal and companion GitHub repositories ('cosylabiiit/Recipedb-companion-data'). No public unrestrained REST API.
candidate_datasets.record_count: >118,000 global recipes; >10,000 traditional Indian recipes spanning 6 regional cuisines
candidate_datasets.food_categories: Complete cooked recipes: Curries, Breads, Rice preparations, Lentils/Dals, Snacks, Desserts, Soups
candidate_datasets.nutrient_basis: Per serving and per total recipe yield (calculated algorithmically via ingredient mapping to USDA / nutritional tables)

nutrient_coverage.micronutrients: Estimated micronutrient breakdown derived from mapped USDA Foundation ingredients.

candidate_datasets.processing_state: Complete cooked multi-ingredient dishes with step-by-step cooking techniques (boiling, sautéing, pressure cooking, deep-frying).
candidate_datasets.recipe_and_portion_support: Full recipe-level support: raw ingredient lists, quantitative measures (grams, teaspoons, cups), serving counts, and cooking instructions.
candidate_datasets.publication_date: 2020 (RecipeDB: Nucleic Acids Research; ongoing laboratory updates)

license_and_legal.official_license: Academic research copyright. Freely accessible for educational and scholarly evaluation. Commercial redistribution or automated bulk scraping for proprietary software is restricted without formal institutional agreement with IIIT-Delhi.
license_and_legal.attribution_requirement: Mandatory citation of academic papers (Batra et al., Nucleic Acids Research 2020).

candidate_datasets.api_limits_and_keys: No public open REST API. Web portal subject to server-side query throttles. Bulk data requires direct academic collaboration.
data_quality_issues: Nutrient values are algorithmic estimates derived by parsing recipe texts and mapping to USDA ingredients; they are NOT laboratory-measured via chemical assays.
Regional cooking variances (oil added for tadka, salt added to taste) lead to significant real-world variance compared to calculated recipe averages.
candidate_datasets.recommended_role: BENCHMARK RECIPE BLUEPRINT ARCHETYPE for developing FitKit's custom Indian Recipe Engine and validating serving sizes.

candidate_datasets.name: Nutritive Value of Indian Foods (NVIF 1989 / 2014) & Cooked Recipe Tables
candidate_datasets.publisher: National Institute of Nutrition (NIN), ICMR - C. Gopalan, B.V. Rama Sastri, S.C. Balasubramanian
candidate_datasets.api_documentation: No official API or digital database. Print monograph / scanned PDF eBook.
formats: Scanned PDF (Table 2: Nutritive Value of Cooked Dishes)
candidate_datasets.record_count: ~850 raw foods, plus ~120 traditional cooked preparations and snacks
candidate_datasets.food_categories: Traditional Indian home-cooked dishes (Idli, Dosa, Chapati, Poori, Upma, Sambar, Rasam, Pongal, Biryani, Dal, Vada)
candidate_datasets.nutrient_basis: Per cooked portion / serving and per 100g of cooked dish

nutrient_coverage.macronutrients: Energy, Moisture, Protein, Fat, Carbohydrate, Ash
nutrient_coverage.micronutrients: Calcium, Phosphorus, Iron, Thiamine, Riboflavin, Niacin, Vitamin C.

candidate_datasets.processing_state: Cooked dishes and preparations tested in ICMR-NIN experimental kitchens.
candidate_datasets.recipe_and_portion_support: Includes standard cooked serving sizes (e.g. 1 Idli = 50g, 1 Chapati = 40g, 1 cup Sambar = 150g).
candidate_datasets.publication_date: 1989 (Reprinted with corrections 2014; superseded for raw foods by IFCT 2017)

license_and_legal.official_license: Copyright © ICMR-NIN. Non-commercial scientific dissemination permitted. Electronic commercial products require written licensing.

data_quality_issues: Superseded chemical assay methods (e.g. Kjeldahl crude protein using 6.25 across all foods instead of species-specific Jones factors; crude fiber instead of enzymatic dietary fiber).
Values represent vintage 1980s recipes which may not reflect modern cooking oils or reduced-fat preparation trends.
candidate_datasets.recommended_role: HISTORICAL SERVING SIZE VALIDATION REFERENCE for standard cooked Indian dish gram weights (Idli, Chapati, Dosa, Sambar).

candidate_datasets.name: FAO/INFOODS Analytical Food Composition Database (AnFooD 2.0) & FCTB
candidate_datasets.publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) of the United Nations / International Network of Food Data Systems
candidate_datasets.record_count: >4,000 analytical records across global/regional tables; includes Food Composition Tables for Bangladesh (FCTB 2013: 381 foods)
candidate_datasets.food_categories: South Asian and tropical agricultural crops, freshwater fishes (Rohu, Hilsa, Catla), pulses, traditional vegetables
candidate_datasets.energy_unit: kJ and kcal reported using standardized INFOODS tagnames

nutrient_coverage.macronutrients: Standardized tagnames: WATER, PROTCNT, FATCE, CHOAVLDF, FIBTG, ASH, ENERC
nutrient_coverage.micronutrients: Full FAO/INFOODS standardized micronutrient profiling with analytical method codes.

candidate_datasets.processing_state: Both raw agricultural crops and selected cooked South Asian preparations.
candidate_datasets.recipe_and_portion_support: Detailed documentation on cooking retention factors and edible portion conversion yields.

license_and_legal.official_license: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 IGO (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO).

data_quality_issues: Non-commercial license prevents direct commercial distribution without UN FAO clearance.
Dispersed across multiple standalone Excel workbooks requiring manual parsing and normalization.
candidate_datasets.recommended_role: SECONDARY VALIDATION SOURCE for South Asian fish species, tropical leafy greens, and international retention factor standardization.

representative_record_audit.serving_measures: Not documented in source (Requires ~40g per cup poha rule)
representative_record_audit.quality_finding: Reported in kJ (1480 kJ / 4.184 = 353.7 kcal). High analytical precision for available carbohydrates via enzymatic method.
Represents dry unhydrated flour. Must not be used directly as cooked paratha/naan without adding cooking oil and water absorption factors.
Exceptionally high dietary fiber (11.18g) and calcium (344 mg/100g verified against IFCT mineral table). Pure raw grain.
High mineral and lipid content compared to rice; raw whole grain.
Raw grain. When converted to Jowar Roti, water absorption increases weight by ~1.35x, reducing energy density per 100g cooked.
Raw dry split pulse. High protein (21.55g) and high dietary fiber (15.15g). When boiled, weight expands ~2.4x.

representative_record_audit.food_name: Red gram, dal (Toor dal / Arhar dal)
representative_record_audit.quality_finding: Primary Indian dal staple. If a user logs '100g Dal' expecting cooked dal but logs this raw profile, they overcount calories by 300% (331 kcal vs ~105 kcal for cooked dal).
Key component of Idli and Dosa batter. Raw dry legume.
High digestibility profile; raw legume.
IFCT reports 12.41g carbohydrate in fresh paneer (lactose retention in curd/whey precipitation). Commercial branded paneer often reports lower carbs (3-7g).

representative_record_audit.serving_measures: Not documented in source (Requires volumetric density conversion: 100ml ≈ 103g)
representative_record_audit.quality_finding: Reported per 100g, not per 100ml. Indian whole cow milk analysis.
Significantly higher fat (7.55g) and calories (107.6 kcal/100g) than cow milk, typical of South Asian buffalo milk.

representative_record_audit.serving_measures: Not documented in source (Requires standard egg weight: ~50g/egg = ~77 kcal)
representative_record_audit.quality_finding: One of only 8 cooked items in IFCT 2017. Values align closely with international reference tables (USDA FDC ID 173424 reports 155 kcal, 12.6g protein).
Raw tuber. Cooking (baking vs deep frying in aloo tikki/pakora) drastically alters fat and calorie profile.
High moisture content (93.21%). Low caloric density staple.
Raw leafy green. Shrinks to ~30-40% volume when wilted/cooked; critical portion-size challenge for home tracking.

representative_record_audit.serving_measures: Not documented in source (Requires volumetric rule: 1 tbsp ≈ 14g ≈ 126 kcal)
representative_record_audit.quality_finding: CRITICAL DATA QUALITY DEFECT: enerc is recorded as 0 in digitized table despite 100g lipid! True value is ~3700 kJ (900 kcal). FitKit must calculate energy via Atwater formula (fat * 9) when enerc is 0.

representative_record_audit.serving_measures: Not documented in source (Requires volumetric rule: 1 tsp ≈ 5g ≈ 45 kcal)
representative_record_audit.quality_finding: CRITICAL DATA QUALITY DEFECT: enerc recorded as 0 in digitized table despite 100g fat. Must be calculated to ~900 kcal.

representative_record_audit.food_name: Rice, white, long-grain, regular, raw, unenriched
representative_record_audit.quality_finding: Raw dry rice profile. Matches IFCT dry grain range (350-365 kcal). Explicit cup gram weight provided.

DEMONSTRATION OF RAW VS COOKED WATER EXPANSION: Cooked rice contains 68.44% water; 100g contains only 130 kcal and 28g carbs compared to raw rice's 365 kcal and 80g carbs. Cooking yield factor ≈ 2.8x.

representative_record_audit.food_name: Chickpeas (garbanzo beans, bengal gram), mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt
representative_record_audit.quality_finding: Cooked pulse profile. Contrast with IFCT B001 raw dal (329 kcal, 21.5g protein); cooked chickpeas contain ~8.9g protein and 164 kcal per 100g due to ~60% water content.
Accurate cooked flatbread entry with piece gram weights. Fat (5.59g) reflects fat/ghee brushed during baking.

representative_record_audit.food_name: Chicken, broilers or fryers, breast, meat only, cooked, roasted
representative_record_audit.quality_finding: Cooked lean meat. Water loss during roasting increases protein concentration to 31.02g/100g (raw chicken breast has ~22g protein/100g).

representative_record_audit.serving_measures: 1 large egg: 50.0g (78 kcal); 1 extra large: 56.0g (87 kcal)
representative_record_audit.quality_finding: Serves as international validation cross-check for IFCT M004 (which reported 153.9 kcal, 13.34g protein).
Commercial packaged formulation with higher fat and lower carbs than fresh artisanal paneer in IFCT L003. Illustrates branded vs generic divergence.
Actual Indian barcode retail record. Lacks comprehensive micronutrient analysis but provides authentic brand-specific nutritional packaging declaration.

data_normalization_rules.energy_standardization: All energy values must be stored internally in both kilocalories (kcal) and kilojoules (kJ). If kcal is missing, calculate via kcal = round(kJ / 4.184, 1). If both energy values are 0 while fat > 0 or protein > 0, calculate energy via Atwater formula: (protein * 4) + (carbs * 4) + (fat * 9) + (fiber * 2).
data_normalization_rules.zero_vs_missing_rule: Missing analytical values must NEVER be coerced to 0. An unmeasured nutrient must be represented as NULL / None with a data_quality_flag = 'UNMEASURED'. Value 0 is reserved strictly for verified zero concentrations (e.g. 0g fiber in refined oil or pure meat).

raw_vs_cooked_distinction.cooking_yield_factors: Cooked_weight = Raw_weight * Yield_Factor. Grains (Rice): 2.5 - 2.8; Pulses (Dal): 2.2 - 2.5; Meats: 0.75 - 0.82 (shrinkage).
raw_vs_cooked_distinction.nutrient_retention_factors: Nutrient_cooked = Nutrient_raw * Retention_Factor. Water-soluble vitamins (C, B-complex) degrade by 15-40% under prolonged boiling; protein and mineral retention remains >90%.

serving_size_hierarchy: 1. Grams / Milliliters (Exact scale weight - Primary anchor)
2. Standardized Household Measures (1 cup = 240ml, 1 tbsp = 15ml, 1 tsp = 5ml)
3. Unit Portions with explicit gram bounds (1 medium Idli = 40-50g, 1 standard Chapati = 35-40g, 1 small Katori = 150g)
